question: Which harmful traditional practice should nurses actively discourage when teaching mothers about diarrhoea?

options.A: Mixing ORS packets in clean drinking water
options.B: Withholding food and fluids to rest the bowel
options.C: Continuing to breastfeed the infant on demand
options.D: Giving zinc supplements for two full weeks

explanation: Never starve a tummy bug! Stopping food and water only makes malnutrition and dehydration worse. Children with diarrhoea need continued feeding and plenty of fluids to heal. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h8)

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care in advanced degenerative disorders?

options.A: Stopping all forms of nursing care
options.B: Curing the genetic disease completely
options.C: Comfort and symptom management
options.D: Increasing rigorous physical therapy

explanation: Palliative care centers on relieving pain and distressing symptoms to ensure the patient remains comfortable and maintains their dignity. Beautiful nursing philosophy! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h8)

question: A young female is being checked for missing internal reproductive organs. What is the best nursing action during her assessment?

options.A: Reviewing her detailed gynecological and developmental medical history
options.B: Preparing her for immediate emergency abdominal surgery
options.C: Administering oral contraceptives to regulate her menstrual flow
options.D: Instructing her to perform daily bimanual pelvic self-examinations

explanation: Taking a thorough history is a core nursing skill! It helps the team understand whether the issue is congenital or acquired. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T28#GNS216_U5_T28_h5)

question: A patient tells you they only want a general idea of their condition and do not want all the technical details. What is the most appropriate nursing response?

options.A: Tell their family members the full medical report instead
options.B: Insist they hear everything so they can make informed choices
options.C: Respect their preference and provide a clear, high-level summary
options.D: Refuse to talk to them until they agree to hear all test results

explanation: Patients have the right to guide how much information they receive, and nurses should honor these individual preferences. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h3)

question: A mum at 28 weeks comes in with a BP of 140/90 mmHg and swollen ankles. What should you do next?

options.A: Perform further evaluation and prepare for possible referral
options.B: Reassure her that swelling is completely normal at all times
options.C: Administer heavy routine sedatives immediately
options.D: Discharge her home with instructions to rest for a week

explanation: You nailed it! High BP and swelling late in pregnancy are red flags for pre-eclampsia that need close checking and quick action. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T15#GNS324_U5_T15_h3)

question: Why is starving or withholding food from a child with diarrhoea a bad idea?

options.A: It stops the kidneys from producing urine
options.B: It triggers immediate bacterial overgrowth
options.C: It delays gut healing and worsens malnutrition
options.D: It causes the child to vomit up all remaining water

explanation: Old myths die hard, but we know better now! Restricting food starves the gut cells, making it harder for the intestines to repair themselves and leading to weight loss. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h5)

question: Which touch receptor is responsible for feeling deep pressure and fast vibrations?

options.A: Pacinian corpuscles
options.B: Meissner corpuscles
options.C: Merkel discs
options.D: Ruffini endings

explanation: You nailed it! Pacinian corpuscles are large, deep receptors built specifically to catch rapid vibrations and heavy pressure. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T5#GNS211_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why is 'dissemination' an important step in surveillance?

options.A: It stops patients from visiting primary health care clinics.
options.B: It permanently deletes old health records to save computer space.
options.C: It ensures feedback is shared with the workers and leaders who need to take action.
options.D: It guarantees that pharmaceutical companies make a profit.

explanation: Dissemination just means sharing the news back. It closes the loop so the people who collected the data and the ones who need to fight the disease are on the same page! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h4)

question: Why is it important to involve traditional and religious leaders in health mobilisation?

options.A: They hold strong moral authority and influence public opinion
options.B: They write the national nursing curriculum
options.C: They are the only people who understand modern medicine
options.D: They are required by law to fund all local pharmacies

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders are respected, and their approval helps community members trust health initiatives. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why is herd immunity so helpful for vulnerable people in a community?

options.A: It guarantees that every single person in the population will develop permanent natural immunity
options.B: It completely eliminates all known environmental reservoirs of a bacterial pathogen
options.C: It transforms live vaccines into safer, non-replicating subunit vaccines
options.D: It reduces overall disease spread, indirectly protecting those who cannot be vaccinated

explanation: Brilliant! When most people are vaccinated, germs struggle to spread, keeping even the unvaccinated safe. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why must a nurse check thyroid levels and ask about substance use when assessing a patient for anxiety?

options.A: Substance use screens are legally required for every psychiatric admission.
options.B: Thyroid hormones directly destroy GABA receptors in the brain.
options.C: Thyroid medications are the primary cure for generalized anxiety disorder.
options.D: Medical conditions and substances can cause physical symptoms that mimic anxiety disorders.

explanation: Brilliant nursing assessment! Things like a hyperactive thyroid or too much caffeine can cause tremors and a racing heart, looking just like anxiety when it's actually something else. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T5#GNS314_U2_T5_h5)

question: How do risk assessment findings help local primary health care centers?

options.A: By allowing them to close down clinics with low patient numbers
options.B: By removing the need to keep paper medical records for patients
options.C: By automatically increasing the monthly salary of the clinic staff
options.D: By guiding them to direct scarce medical supplies where most needed

explanation: Resources are usually limited in our clinics. Clear data helps community nurses send drugs and mosquito nets precisely where the greatest need is. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h2)

question: What is the primary contribution of local health workers to a school health programme?

options.A: Providing clinical expertise and conducting health screenings
options.B: Drafting the national educational curriculum for science
options.C: Enforcing school discipline and attendance policies
options.D: Building new classroom blocks and administrative offices

explanation: Nurses and community health extension workers bring professional medical knowledge to evaluate student health and manage basic interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the name of the first nutrient-rich, antibody-packed milk a mother produces after birth?

options.A: Colostrum
options.B: Surfactant
options.C: Meconium
options.D: Lochia

explanation: Colostrum is liquid gold for the newborn! It is packed with antibodies to protect the baby before the regular milk comes in. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h4)

question: Who should you use standard precautions for in the ward?

options.A: All patients receiving care regardless of diagnosis
options.B: Visitors and administrative staff members only
options.C: Patients admitted specifically to isolation wards
options.D: Only patients with confirmed infectious diseases

explanation: Great job! Standard precautions are meant for EVERY patient, every single time. Since we don't always know who might be carrying an infection, treating everyone with these safety rules keeps both you and your patients safe. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h1)

question: Why are community health nurses in the best position to spot social needs in physical disability cases?

options.A: They possess formal training in civil engineering and urban planning
options.B: They manage all legal court cases regarding disability discrimination
options.C: They regularly visit homes, schools, and local community settings
options.D: They have the sole authority to approve government building budgets

explanation: Correct! Because community nurses visit homes and local areas, they see real-life challenges that clinic visits miss. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T11#GNS225_U5_T11_h6)

question: Oops! During insertion, your catheter accidentally slips into the female vagina. What should you do next?

options.A: Wash the same catheter with antiseptic soap and try again
options.B: Leave it temporarily as a landmark and insert a new sterile catheter
options.C: Push it deeper into the vagina to find the correct opening
options.D: Remove it and immediately push that same tube into the urethral meatus

explanation: Smart nursing move! Leaving that stray tube in the vagina stops you from accidentally making the same mistake twice on your next try. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T21#GNS212_U1_T21_h2)

question: What term describes the guilt and emotional trauma healthcare workers feel after an adverse event?

options.A: Primary clinical burnout
options.B: Second victim syndrome
options.C: Professional apathy disorder
options.D: Acute diagnostic fatigue

explanation: We call healthcare workers 'second victims' when they suffer deep emotional distress and trauma after a clinical error. [learn more](GST319_U6_T3#GST319_U6_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary focus of a midwife's professional practice?

options.A: Diagnosing and treating chronic non-communicable diseases
options.B: Managing complex surgical procedures in tertiary hospitals
options.C: Providing care during pregnancy, labor, and the postpartum period
options.D: Administering pediatric vaccinations exclusively

explanation: Midwives specialize in supporting women through pregnancy, childbirth, and the postnatal stage. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h1)

question: A patient's barium swallow report mentions a pouch-like herniation of the mucosal wall in the upper throat area. Which condition matches this description?

options.A: Gastroesophageal reflux
options.B: Esophageal carcinoma
options.C: Sliding hiatal hernia
options.D: Zenker's diverticulum

explanation: A Zenker's diverticulum is an outpouching that occurs in the pharyngoesophageal junction, trapping food particles and causing regurgitation. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h6)

question: How can stagnant water or soil act as a source of community infection?

options.A: By attracting human carriers to contaminated areas
options.B: By turning into clinical cases of human disease
options.C: By harboring environmental bacteria and fungal spores that enter the body
options.D: By mutating human cells to create new viruses

explanation: Soil and water can hold onto tough bacteria and spores. When people come into contact with them through breaks in the skin or swallowing, an infection can start. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is getting an autoimmune disease diagnosed often a long and tricky journey?

options.A: Blood tests are completely unavailable for most autoimmune conditions
options.B: Early symptoms are vague, overlapping, and resemble many other common illnesses
options.C: Autoimmune markers change completely every single day
options.D: Patients rarely report their symptoms to healthcare providers early on

explanation: Early signs like tiredness and body aches look like everyday malaria or stress, making it tough for doctors to pin down right away. [learn more](GST114_U4_T8#GST114_U4_T8_h5)

question: What is the very first thing that happens when a person starts developing an illness?

options.A: Seeking medical care
options.B: Experiencing symptoms
options.C: Entering rehabilitation
options.D: Assuming the sick role

explanation: Easy and logical! The illness journey always starts when the person physically or mentally notices that something feels off in their body. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary function of carbohydrates in the human body?

options.A: To build strong bones and teeth
options.B: To transport oxygen in the blood
options.C: To provide the body's primary and most efficient source of energy
options.D: To repair damaged skin tissue

explanation: Carbohydrates break down into glucose, which fuels the brain, organs, and muscles for daily activities. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T005#GNS227_U1_T005_h2)

question: Who are key local figures nurses should partner with to improve community trust during an outbreak?

options.A: International tourists visiting the country
options.B: Traditional rulers and religious leaders
options.C: Commercial transport drivers only
options.D: Private company directors from abroad

explanation: Local leaders hold immense influence and help relay public health messages effectively within their communities. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h8)

question: A patient says they cannot afford the expensive imported supplements prescribed elsewhere. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Report the patient to the hospital management
options.B: Tell the patient to stop eating altogether
options.C: Tell them to borrow money to buy the brand
options.D: Help the patient find affordable local whole-food alternatives

explanation: Brilliant! As a nurse, you bridge the gap by showing patients how to get great nutrition using what is easily available around them. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T5#GNS216_U6_T5_h8)

question: What is the main job of the lactiferous sinuses when a mother is breastfeeding?

options.A: They produce the hormone prolactin for milk synthesis
options.B: They filter waste products out of the breast milk
options.C: They secrete lubricating oils to protect the areola
options.D: They temporarily store milk before it reaches the nipple

explanation: Think of lactiferous sinuses as little holding pools right under the dark part of the breast (areola). They keep milk ready right where the baby can easily draw it out. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T10#GNS121_U7_T10_h1)

question: Why do we have to be extra careful when disposing of cytotoxic (chemotherapy) drugs?

options.A: Expired tablets turn into sweet-tasting candy that attracts children
options.B: These drugs instantly catch fire when exposed to ordinary air
options.C: Cytotoxic drugs are designed to destroy cells and can damage healthy tissue and genetic material
options.D: Chemotherapy drugs make the local soil extremely fertile for crops

explanation: Spot on! These medications are specially made to kill fast-growing cells, meaning they can harm healthy human tissue and our environment if carelessly thrown out. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h4)

question: A community health nurse is teaching a mother how to improve her family's protein intake using affordable local foods. What is the best advice?

options.A: Combine local plant sources like beans and maize to get complete proteins
options.B: Feed the family exclusively imported vitamin pills instead of meals
options.C: Avoid all local staple carbohydrates like yam and cassava completely
options.D: Rely only on expensive red meat imported from overseas

explanation: Pairing local plant foods like beans and maize gives you a complete protein combo without breaking the bank. Brilliant nursing care! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T005#GNS227_U4_T005_h7)

question: A patient from a large extended family is admitted to the ward. What are you most likely to observe?

options.A: Complete isolation with zero visitors due to strict rules
options.B: Immediate legal action to discharge the patient
options.C: Many relatives visiting, offering opinions, and sharing caregiving duties
options.D: Total reliance on hospital staff for basic feeding and hygiene tasks

explanation: In Nigeria, extended families are wonderfully close-knit and rally round to support a sick member during hospitalization. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which condition is a primary indication for a low salt diet in hospital wards?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Acute bone fractures
options.C: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Hypertension is directly linked to sodium intake, making salt restriction a primary medical intervention for high blood pressure. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h3)

question: Which of these is a classic geriatric syndrome often managed in long-term care?

options.A: Acute appendicitis
options.B: Bacterial meningitis
options.C: Pressure injuries
options.D: Compound fractures

explanation: Keep shining! Pressure injuries, falls, and confusion are common multi-factorial challenges we look out for in frail older adults. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h4)

question: When is the best time to put a newborn baby to the breast for the very first time?

options.A: Only when the mother's milk turns white
options.B: After twenty-four hours of observation
options.C: Within the first hour after birth
options.D: Once the baby cries continuously

explanation: You nailed it! Starting breastfeeding within that first hour helps boost milk flow and gives the baby that precious, protective colostrum. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h3)

question: How do recurring illnesses like malaria lead to childhood malnutrition?

options.A: By directly destroying the child's bone marrow and skeleton
options.B: By changing the color of breast milk in the mother's body
options.C: By forcing the child to sleep longer hours during the day
options.D: By increasing nutrient demand while reducing the child's appetite

explanation: Fever and sickness make the body burn more energy, but sick kids usually don't want to eat. That combination leads straight to weight loss. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h7)

question: What is the absolute first priority when managing any acute poisoning patient in the emergency unit?

options.A: Securing the airway and ensuring adequate breathing
options.B: Collecting urine samples for toxicological screening
options.C: Inducing immediate vomiting to empty the stomach
options.D: Administering activated charcoal via nasogastric tube

explanation: Always fall back on your ABCDEs! Life support and stabilization always come way before diagnostic tests or trying to remove the poison. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h6)

question: What makes the Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV) so great for massive community campaigns?

options.A: It is given through an injection that leaves a lasting scar
options.B: It contains live bacteria that cure existing paralysis
options.C: It does not require any temperature control or refrigeration
options.D: It is simple to administer and builds good gut immunity

explanation: Brilliant! Drops are easy to give without needing injection pros, and they build strong defense right where the virus enters—the gut. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h5)

question: How does a hospital's poor response to a nursing mistake affect the rest of the team?

options.A: It immediately prevents all future near misses
options.B: It improves patient trust in hospital management
options.C: It drives staff to leave the profession out of fear and burnout
options.D: It encourages open communication and total honesty

explanation: When hospitals rely on blame and punishment instead of support, staff live in fear, leading to burnout and nursing shortages. We need supportive wards! [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h6)

question: What is the very first thing you should do when setting new objectives for a healthcare unit?

options.A: Punish staff members who failed previous targets.
options.B: Purchase expensive new medical equipment for the ward.
options.C: Assess current performance using past data and audit reports.
options.D: Rewrite the entire hospital mission statement.

explanation: Before moving forward, we always check where we currently stand by reviewing past records and audits to see what needs fixing. [learn more](GST321_U2_T1#GST321_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which classroom setup helps prevent you from feeling sleepy during long lectures?

options.A: Bright neon paint and loud music
options.B: Proper lighting and good ventilation
options.C: Complete darkness with shut windows
options.D: Tight, cramped seating to save space

explanation: Fresh air and good lighting keep headaches and sleepiness away, helping you stay sharp and focused while your lecturer is talking. [learn more](GST321_U8_T3#GST321_U8_T3_h2)

question: What are the two core behavioral areas used to understand autism?

options.A: Aggressive outbursts and profound sleepiness
options.B: Social communication challenges and repetitive behaviors
options.C: Hyperactivity and attention deficits
options.D: Memory loss and sudden physical paralysis

explanation: Spot on! Autism is primarily identified by differences in how a person communicates socially, alongside a preference for repetitive routines or movements. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T5#GNS324_U4_T5_h2)

question: How does home care primarily reduce patient anxiety compared to hospital stays?

options.A: By keeping patients in a familiar environment near loved ones and daily routines
options.B: By guaranteeing that doctors visit the home every single hour
options.C: By stopping family members from visiting during stressful treatment times
options.D: By eliminating the need for any medications or painful procedures

explanation: Familiar surroundings and personal routines help lower stress and confusion for recovering patients. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why is chronic glomerulonephritis often discovered quite late?

options.A: It develops silently over many years before symptoms show
options.B: Lab tests cannot detect kidney problems early
options.C: Symptoms only appear after dialysis starts
options.D: Patients always ignore early severe pain

explanation: Spot on! The disease moves so slowly that the healthy parts of the kidneys work extra hard to cover for the damaged parts, hiding the problem for a long time. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T5#GNS213_U4_T5_h1)

question: What does the glycemic index (GI) measure about a carbohydrate food?

options.A: The amount of sodium added during processing
options.B: How much total fiber is in the serving
options.C: How fast and high it raises blood sugar
options.D: The exact number of calories it contains

explanation: The glycemic index ranks foods by their speed and intensity in raising blood glucose levels. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h3)

question: Which crucial supplement do nurses always advise early pregnant mothers to take to prevent spinal and brain birth defects?

options.A: Folic acid
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Calcium carbonate
options.D: Iron sulfate

explanation: Folic acid is a superstar vitamin for early pregnancy! It protects the baby's developing neural tube from serious defects. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T002#GNS226_U2_T002_h7)

question: During passive range of motion exercises, who is responsible for moving the joint?

options.A: The physical therapist using electrical stimulation
options.B: The nurse or caregiver moves the limb
options.C: The patient uses their own muscle strength
options.D: A mechanical pulley system driven by gravity

explanation: Remember, in *passive* exercises, the patient's muscles aren't doing the work—you (the nurse or helper) gently move the joints for them to keep them flexible. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h4)

question: A nurse wants to test a new handwashing routine on two existing hospital wards without disrupting shift schedules. Which design fits best?

options.A: Quasi-experimental design
options.B: Historical research design
options.C: Phenomenological design
options.D: True experimental design

explanation: Spot on! When you have to use existing groups (like pre-formed wards) instead of mixing everyone randomly, you are doing a quasi-experiment. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T3#GNS224_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is a big drawback of looking only at hospital records to assess a community's health?

options.A: It only includes data about elderly male patients
options.B: It misses people who cannot afford or access hospital care
options.C: It takes too much time for the nursing staff to read
options.D: It contains too many details about infectious diseases

explanation: Exactly. Hospital records only capture those who manage to reach the facility, leaving out the many sick people stuck at home due to distance or poverty. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h2)

question: Which injection site symptom means the patient needs to call a doctor right away?

options.A: A small pinprick dot of dry blood on the skin surface
options.B: Pus drainage, severe pain, and spreading warmth
options.C: Temporary slight coolness where the alcohol dried
options.D: Mild fading skin discoloration from a tiny bruise

explanation: Those are classic red flags for an infection! Pus, severe pain, and warmth mean the site needs medical attention quickly. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h7)

question: What usually happens in healthcare facilities that ignore employee aspirations for rigid administrative targets?

options.A: High rates of staff resignation, burnout, and medical errors
options.B: Zero complaints from patients and staff members
options.C: Automatic salary increases for all junior nursing staff
options.D: Immediate recognition as the best hospital in the country

explanation: When a hospital treats staff like robots and ignores their personal growth, nurses get burnt out, resign, and mistakes can easily happen in patient care. [learn more](GST321_U2_T2#GST321_U2_T2_h8)

question: What emergency item must always be kept right at the bedside after an amputation surgery?

options.A: A heating pad
options.B: A tourniquet
options.C: An extra pillow
options.D: A bedside commode

explanation: A tourniquet is kept at the bedside just in case there is sudden, heavy bleeding from the surgical site that needs immediate stopping. Safety first! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h3)

question: Students vomit and have stomach pain after eating snacks from an outside vendor near the gate. What should be done urgently?

options.A: Increasing the academic workload to distract students from illness
options.B: Replacing all classroom desks and chairs with new furniture
options.C: Inspecting and regulating food hygiene practices around the school
options.D: Canceling all physical education classes for the remainder of the term

explanation: Great job! Food poisoning from external sellers means health authorities need to step in and check food safety standards fast. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why do we check baseline blood tests before starting certain tricky medications?

options.A: They prevent the drug from causing stomach irritation
options.B: They prove whether the patient has an active drug allergy
options.C: They provide a reference point to catch early organ damage
options.D: They calculate the exact lethal dose for that individual

explanation: Baselines give us a 'before' picture so we can quickly spot if a drug starts harming organs later. Brilliant nursing practice! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T7#GNS125_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why do we frequently check a U&E panel when a patient is receiving intravenous fluids?

options.A: To monitor changes in kidney function and body salts
options.B: To measure the exact oxygen level in the veins
options.C: To check if the patient is developing an infection
options.D: To screen the patient for inherited blood disorders

explanation: You've got this! Giving IV fluids changes the balance of water and minerals in the body. The U&E panel helps us track these changes to keep our patients safe and stable. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T9#GNS123_U2_T9_h1)

question: When is the second medication safety check typically performed?

options.A: While preparing or pouring the medication
options.B: When removing the drug from the storage shelf
options.C: During the morning nursing handover meeting
options.D: After the patient has swallowed the pill

explanation: The second check happens during preparation to ensure the right drug and dose are being measured out correctly. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h5)

question: When mistakes happen in the clinic, what is usually the real root cause?

options.A: Flawed system designs interacting with human limits
options.B: Poor physical fitness and lack of sleep
options.C: A lack of basic nursing education among staff
options.D: Intentional negligence by individual healthcare workers

explanation: You're doing great! Remember that most clinical errors happen because the work environment and tools don't properly support natural human limits—not because nurses are careless. [learn more](GST319_U5_T8#GST319_U5_T8_h1)

question: What is the primary maternal health benefit of properly spacing pregnancies?

options.A: Permanently stopping all future menstrual cycles
options.B: Eliminating the need for any antenatal care visits
options.C: Giving the mother's body time to recover physically
options.D: Ensuring the mother gives birth only to male children

explanation: Proper spacing allows a woman's body to restore vital nutrients like iron and heal from the physical stress of a previous pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h1)

question: Why does long-term low blood oxygen sometimes lead to secondary polycythemia?

options.A: The liver releases clotting factors to repair damaged alveolar walls
options.B: The bone marrow responds to inflammation by producing excess white blood cells
options.C: The body tries to carry more oxygen by making extra red blood cells
options.D: Dehydrated blood vessels concentrate the existing red blood cells rapidly

explanation: You're nailing this! Making extra red blood cells is the body's clever way of packing more oxygen-carriers into the blood when air supply is low. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h7)

question: Why are both FSH and testosterone needed for normal sperm production in males?

options.A: Because both hormones are actually identical chemical substances made by the liver
options.B: Because FSH supports the supporting cells while testosterone drives the overall development
options.C: Because testosterone fights off infections while FSH controls body temperature
options.D: Because FSH stops the growth of body hair while testosterone makes bones brittle

explanation: Exactly right! FSH supports the helper cells (Sertoli cells), while testosterone provides the fuel needed for sperm cells to fully mature. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T13#GNS121_U5_T13_h5)

question: What is the main role of a home care nurse when working with the healthcare team on a slow-healing wound?

options.A: Acting as the eyes and ears to report accurate, up-to-date wound changes to providers
options.B: Ordering all prescription medications without physician approval
options.C: Performing surgical debridement during every home visit
options.D: Diagnosing the underlying systemic disease independently

explanation: You are the vital link! Your accurate updates from the home help doctors, dietitians, and specialists adjust the care plan so the patient heals faster. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why is the intraarticular route preferred for treating a single inflamed joint?

options.A: It prevents any risk of local infection at the injection site
options.B: It is completely painless compared to taking oral medications
options.C: It completely cures chronic arthritis after just one single dose

question: What is the main goal of public health laws for food businesses?

question: Why is working closely with local and religious leaders so vital for successful immunization drives?

question: What do we call the type of laryngoscopy that uses a thin, flexible camera passed through the nose?

question: Why is it helpful to raise the head of the bed slightly when sliding a bedpan under a patient?

question: What should you do if you spot an item on the sterile table and you are not totally sure if it is sterile?

question: What are early warning signs of a psychiatric relapse?

question: You notice a fellow nurse showing signs of severe impairment while on duty. What is the best professional step to take?

question: What is Faget's sign, a unique finding nurses watch for in yellow fever patients?

question: What is the very first check a nurse must perform before giving any medication?

question: What does a line that slopes upward on a healthcare chart tell you?

question: Roughly how long is the plasma half-life of levothyroxine in a healthy person?

question: What is the main purpose of using a Punnett square?

question: Why are LARC methods considered very effective for post-abortion contraception?

options.B: A broken chain of infection
options.C: A mode of transmission for pathogens
options.D: A sterile clinical environment

explanation: Oops! Skipping hand hygiene turned the nurse's hands into a taxi service for germs, moving them straight to a vulnerable spot. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h3)

question: What does evidence-based nursing practice combine with research evidence?

options.A: Traditional hospital routines from the past
options.B: Financial costs of medical equipment
options.C: Personal opinions of the hospital director
options.D: Clinical expertise and patient values

explanation: True evidence-based practice brings together research findings, the nurse's clinical judgment, and the preferences of the patient. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the main goal of disease prevention in public health?

options.A: Finding new surgical methods for complex chronic illnesses
options.B: Stopping health problems before they start or halting their progress
options.C: Reducing the cost of pharmaceutical manufacturing plants
options.D: Increasing hospital admission rates for routine checkups

explanation: You've got this! Prevention is all about stopping illness proactively before it takes hold, rather than just treating symptoms later. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h1)

question: Why is the old saying 'eating for two' a bit misleading for expectant mothers?

options.A: It suggests that pregnant women need fewer calories than non-pregnant women
options.B: It encourages doubling food quantity rather than focusing on nutrient quality
options.C: It means the baby eats solid food while still inside the womb
options.D: It applies only to the final month of the pregnancy period

explanation: It's not about eating twice as much food! It's about making smarter, nutrient-packed food choices so both you and baby get the right vitamins. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T012#GNS227_U2_T012_h1)

question: Which type of waste must be burned at very high temperatures instead of just going into an autoclave?

options.A: Cardboard medication delivery boxes
options.B: Empty intravenous fluid plastic bags
options.C: Pathological waste and human tissues
options.D: Uncontaminated paper paperwork

explanation: Anatomical parts and human tissues require high-temperature incineration for safety and out of respect for human dignity. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h6)

question: A female patient keeps coming to the clinic with ongoing tummy upsets and pelvic pain, but tests show no physical illness. What should the nurse keep in mind?

options.A: A congenital malformation of the gastrointestinal tract
options.B: History of unaddressed gender-based violence and chronic stress
options.C: An acute bacterial infection requiring high-dose antibiotics
options.D: Normal physiological adaptation to routine aging processes

explanation: Brilliant thinking! Emotional and physical trauma often show up as recurring body pains when medical tests can't find a direct physical cause. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T8#GNS312_U4_T8_h4)

question: What type of liability do nurse managers usually face if they do a poor job with staffing or hiring?

options.A: Strict criminal liability for patient readmissions
options.B: Direct liability for administrative negligence
options.C: Absolute immunity from all civil court proceedings
options.D: Vicarious liability for every bedside drug error

explanation: Managers have specific administrative duties like vetting staff properly. If they fail here, they face direct liability for their own poor management. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h6)

question: What is the main goal of psychiatric rehabilitation?

options.A: To keep patients in hospital care permanently
options.B: To isolate patients from their families forever
options.C: To cure mental illness using only herbal remedies
options.D: To help patients return to meaningful community life

explanation: You got this! Psychiatric rehabilitation is all about helping individuals with long-term mental health challenges regain their independence and live fulfilling lives back in society. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h1)

question: What is the main difference between being 'gifted' and having a 'talent'?

options.A: Giftedness is general mental potential while talent is specific performance.
options.B: Talent appears in early childhood whereas giftedness appears in adolescence.
options.C: Giftedness relies on physical skill while talent relies on memory.
options.D: Talent requires formal testing whereas giftedness develops naturally.

explanation: You've got this! Think of giftedness as a broad, overall high intellectual ability, while talent is when someone shines brightly in one specific area, like music or math. Keep going! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T1#GNS225_U5_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is an example of primary data collection?

options.A: Reviewing old hospital admission registers in the record room
options.B: Conducting house-to-house surveys and interviews with residents
options.C: Reading national census reports published ten years ago
options.D: Downloading international World Health Organization PDF reports

explanation: Primary data is gathered directly from the source by the healthcare worker conducting the investigation. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h3)

question: What famous milestone did James Lind achieve when he tested citrus fruits on sailors?

options.A: The chemical isolation of pure vitamin C in a laboratory
options.B: The creation of the first national food pyramid
options.C: An early controlled clinical trial using citrus fruits for scurvy
options.D: The discovery of complex carbohydrates in grains

explanation: You nailed it! Lind compared different treatments and proved that oranges and lemons could cure sailors suffering from scurvy. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h3)
